sources.publisher: Income Tax Department, Ministry of Finance
sources.title: Power to condone delay in filing Form No. 10A under section 12A(1)(ac)(i)
sources.applicability: Trusts and institutions that filed Form 10A late and have a condonation application pending or filed on or after the circular date.
sources.seedText: CBDT clarifies that the jurisdictional Principal Commissioner or Commissioner of Income-tax has power to condone delay in filing Form 10A under section 12A(1)(ac)(i). The circular applies where Form 10A was filed late and the condonation application is pending or is filed on or after the circular date.

sources.publisher: Income Tax Department, Ministry of Finance
sources.title: Extension for issuing TDS certificates for the quarter ended 31 December 2025
sources.applicability: Deductors issuing TDS certificates under section 203 read with rule 31 for the quarter ended 31 December 2025.
sources.seedText: For the quarter ended 31 December 2025, CBDT extended the due date for issuing TDS certificates under section 203 read with rule 31 to 31 March 2026 because of e-filing portal technical glitches. This was a one-time extension and is now historical.

sources.publisher: Income Tax Department, Ministry of Finance
sources.title: Forms for notification and quarterly reporting by Sovereign Wealth Funds
sources.applicability: Sovereign wealth funds seeking or holding notification under Schedule V of the Income-tax Act, 2025.
sources.seedText: CBDT specifies Form I for a sovereign wealth fund seeking notification and Form II for quarterly reporting of investments. An already-notified fund does not file a fresh Form I but must file Form II within one month after each quarter. The circular is effective from 1 April 2026 for tax year 2026-27 and later years.

sources.publisher: Income Tax Department, Ministry of Finance
sources.title: Condonation of delay in electronically filing Form No. 10AB for approval under section 80G(5)
sources.applicability: Applicants seeking approval under clause (ii) of the first proviso to section 80G(5) whose Form 10AB was filed late.
sources.seedText: Official CBDT publication concerning condonation of delay in electronically filing Form 10AB for approval under clause (ii) of the first proviso to section 80G(5). The source page identifies it as Circular No. 6/2026 dated 2 July 2026. The circular text must be checked before advising on eligibility or procedure.

sources.publisher: Income Tax Department, Ministry of Finance
sources.title: CBDT circulars index
sources.applicability: Discovery and freshness verification for CBDT circulars; not sufficient by itself for a legal conclusion.
sources.seedText: Official CBDT circulars index used to discover new publications and verify that a retrieved circular remains current. Open the underlying circular before relying on a substantive conclusion.

sources.publisher: Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs
sources.title: DIN requirement for GST common-portal communications carrying a verifiable RFN
sources.applicability: CBIC communications generated through the GST common portal under section 169 that carry a verifiable Reference Number.
sources.seedText: CBIC clarifies that a communication generated through the GST common portal under section 169 and bearing a verifiable RFN does not also require a DIN. The RFN-bearing communication is valid. Circulars 122/41/2019-GST and 128/47/2019-GST stand modified to that extent.

sources.publisher: Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs
sources.title: Review, revision and appeal for orders passed by Common Adjudicating Authorities
sources.applicability: Orders-in-Original passed by a Common Adjudicating Authority for show-cause notices issued by DGGI.
sources.seedText: For orders passed by a Common Adjudicating Authority, the Principal Commissioner or Commissioner under whom that authority is posted is the reviewing authority under section 107 and the revisional authority under section 108. Appeals lie to the Commissioner (Appeals) corresponding to that territorial jurisdiction.

sources.publisher: Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs
sources.title: CBIC central GST circulars index
sources.applicability: Discovery and freshness verification for central GST circulars; not sufficient by itself for a legal conclusion.
sources.seedText: Official CBIC index for central GST circulars. Use it to discover newer circulars and to check number, date and subject, then open the underlying circular before relying on a conclusion.

sources.publisher: Goods and Services Tax Network
sources.title: Form GSTR-1 user manual
sources.applicability: Registered persons preparing or filing outward-supply details in Form GSTR-1 on the GST portal.
sources.seedText: Official GST portal user manual for preparing, saving, previewing and filing Form GSTR-1. Portal instructions support the mechanics of filing but do not by themselves determine legal applicability or a tax position.

sources.publisher: Goods and Services Tax Network
sources.title: GST welcome kit and GSTR-3B filing guidance
sources.applicability: Registered persons using the GST portal for return preparation and payment.
sources.seedText: Official GSTN guidance for new taxpayers covering core portal workflows, return preparation and payment. Treat portal guidance as procedural support and verify current due dates or legal positions against the current notification or circular.

sources.publisher: Income Tax Department, Government of India
sources.title: Tax payment and TDS payment frequently asked questions
sources.applicability: Taxpayers and deductors using the Income Tax e-filing portal for tax payments.
sources.seedText: Official e-filing portal help for tax payments. Use it for current portal mechanics and payment troubleshooting, while checking the Act, Rules and applicable CBDT publication for the underlying obligation and deadline.

sources.publisher: Income Tax Department, Government of India
sources.title: ITR-1 online filing and advance-tax guidance
sources.applicability: Individuals evaluating ITR-1 eligibility or using the e-filing portal, subject to statutory eligibility conditions.
sources.seedText: Official e-filing guidance on ITR-1 filing and related payment steps. Confirm form eligibility and the substantive tax position against the current Act, Rules, instructions and notifications.

sources.publisher: Institute of Chartered Accountants of India
sources.title: Deferment of the mandatory effective date of SQM 1 and SQM 2
sources.applicability: Firms performing audits, reviews, assurance or related-services engagements under ICAI standards.
sources.seedText: ICAI deferred the mandatory effective date of SQM 1 and SQM 2, which had been scheduled for 1 April 2026, until a further announcement. SQC 1 continues to remain in force and applicable in the meantime. The announcement was issued under the authority of the ICAI Council.

sources.publisher: Institute of Chartered Accountants of India
sources.title: Guidance Note on Audit of Banks — 2026 edition
sources.applicability: Members conducting statutory audits of banks for the relevant audit cycle.
sources.seedText: Official ICAI landing page for the 2026 edition of the Guidance Note on Audit of Banks. Use the linked complete guidance note and the engagement's applicable RBI directions and auditing standards before reaching an audit conclusion.

sources.publisher: Institute of Chartered Accountants of India
sources.title: ICAI Accounting Standards index
sources.applicability: Discovery of ICAI Accounting Standards; applicability depends on the reporting framework, entity and period.
sources.seedText: Official ICAI Accounting Standards index. Retrieve the full current standard and check the entity's reporting framework and period before applying a recognition, measurement, presentation or disclosure conclusion.

sources.publisher: Institute of Chartered Accountants of India
sources.title: ICAI Auditing and Assurance Standards Board resources
sources.applicability: Discovery of engagement and quality-control standards, guidance notes and AASB announcements.
sources.seedText: Official ICAI Auditing and Assurance Standards Board resource page. Use it to locate the complete applicable standard, guidance note and current announcement for the engagement.

sources.publisher: Securities and Exchange Board of India
sources.title: SEBI circulars index
sources.applicability: Discovery and freshness verification for active SEBI circulars across regulated intermediaries.
sources.seedText: Official SEBI active-circular index. At the latest recorded check it contained current 2026 circulars. Use it to discover later publications and open the underlying circular before relying on any compliance conclusion.

sources.publisher: Securities and Exchange Board of India
sources.title: SEBI master circulars index
sources.applicability: Discovery of consolidated SEBI master circulars; confirm subsequent amendments from the active circular index.
sources.seedText: Official SEBI master-circular index. A master circular consolidates material to its stated cut-off date; later circulars can amend it, so check the active circular index as well.

sources.publisher: Securities and Exchange Board of India
sources.title: Special window for transfer and dematerialisation of physical securities
sources.applicability: Holders, listed entities, RTAs and intermediaries dealing with eligible physical-securities transfer cases described in the circular.
sources.seedText: Official SEBI circular dated 30 January 2026 concerning a special window for specified physical-securities transfer and dematerialisation cases. Read the complete circular to confirm eligibility, window dates, documentary conditions and intermediary responsibilities.

sources.publisher: Employees' Provident Fund Organisation
sources.title: EPFO employer and contribution frequently asked questions
sources.applicability: Establishments and employers covered by the EPF & MP Act and schemes.
sources.seedText: Official EPFO frequently asked questions. The employer must electronically file wage-month information through ECR and, under paragraph 38(1), pay contributions within fifteen days after the close of the month. Verify any temporary relief, extension or portal change against a current EPFO publication.

sources.publisher: Reserve Bank of India
sources.title: Qualifying Assets Criteria for Non-Banking Financial Company — Micro Finance Institutions
sources.applicability: Non-Banking Financial Company — Micro Finance Institutions and their qualifying-assets classification under the applicable RBI regulatory framework.
sources.seedText: RBI/2025-26/44 dated 6 June 2025 prescribes that an NBFC-MFI must maintain qualifying assets constituting at least sixty per cent of its total assets, net of intangible assets, on an ongoing basis. The circular states that the instructions take immediate effect. Read the complete RBI publication and applicable Master Direction before concluding on classification.

sources.publisher: Reserve Bank of India
sources.title: Compliance Function and Role of Chief Compliance Officer in NBFCs
sources.applicability: Upper Layer and Middle Layer NBFCs within the scope and implementation timetable stated in the RBI circular.
sources.seedText: Official RBI circular on an independent compliance function and the role of the Chief Compliance Officer in specified NBFCs. Applicability and implementation timing differ by NBFC layer. Use the complete circular to verify board responsibilities, appointment criteria, tenure, reporting line and review requirements.

sources.publisher: Ministry of Corporate Affairs, Government of India
sources.title: The Companies Act, 2013
sources.applicability: Companies and other persons or matters within the provisions of the Companies Act, subject to commencement notifications, later amendments, rules and exemptions.
sources.seedText: Official MCA text of the Companies Act, 2013. A conclusion must also account for the relevant provision's commencement, later amending Acts, applicable rules, exemptions, notifications and MCA circulars; the base Act alone is not a complete statement of every current company-law obligation.

sources.publisher: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India
sources.title: FSSAI Advisories and Orders index
sources.applicability: Discovery and freshness verification for FSSAI advisories and orders; the underlying publication controls.
sources.seedText: Official FSSAI Advisories and Orders index. Use it to find later publications and open the complete underlying advisory or order before relying on a compliance conclusion.

sources.publisher: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India
sources.title: FSSAI Gazette Notifications index
sources.applicability: Discovery and freshness verification for FSSAI regulations and amendment notifications; the gazetted instrument controls.
sources.seedText: Official FSSAI Gazette Notifications index. Use it to identify the complete gazetted regulation, its commencement clause and subsequent amendments before applying a legal requirement.

sources.publisher: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India
sources.title: Enforcement against prohibited use of calcium carbide and unsafe ethylene in artificial ripening of fruits
sources.applicability: Food business operators, fruit traders, ripening facilities and enforcement officials involved in artificial ripening of fruits.
sources.seedText: FSSAI's advisory dated 16 April 2026 reiterates that calcium carbide is prohibited for artificial ripening under Regulation 2.3.5 and that direct contact of fruits with ethylene in powder or liquid form is prohibited. It directs inspection and enforcement activity. Read the full advisory for the prescribed handling, chamber and enforcement guidance.

sources.publisher: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India
sources.title: Food Safety and Standards (Licensing and Registration of Food Businesses) Amendment Regulations, 2026
sources.applicability: Food business operators, petty food businesses, street food vendors and licensing authorities within the amended regulations.
sources.seedText: The 2026 amendment revises licensing and registration requirements, including treatment of specified street food vendors, continuity of licences and registrations unless suspended, cancelled or surrendered, consequences tied to annual fees or returns, a thirty-day closure-intimation requirement and risk-based inspection or audit provisions. Apply the exact amended text and transition provisions to the food business concerned.

sources.publisher: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India
sources.title: Food Safety and Standards (Licensing and Registration of Food Businesses) Second Amendment Regulations, 2026
sources.applicability: Food business operators subject to the amended production, raw-material and storage-record requirements, with stated exceptions.
sources.seedText: The FSSAI Second Amendment Regulations, 2026 introduce record requirements for manufacturing food business operators and storage controls including first-in-first-out or first-expiry-first-out principles, subject to the text's scope and exceptions. Confirm the gazette date and exact commencement clause from the complete notification before setting a compliance deadline.

sources.publisher: Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs
sources.title: The Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 (full text as enacted)
sources.applicability: All persons registered or liable to be registered under GST; governs levy, input tax credit, returns, late fee, interest, demands and service of notice under central GST law.
sources.seedText: Official CBIC page carrying the complete English text of the Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017, including the chapters on levy and collection, input tax credit (section 16 conditions for availing ITC), returns, demands and recovery, and service of notice. Section 47 (Levy of late fee) prescribes one hundred rupees for each day a return under section 39 or 45 remains unfiled, subject to a cap. Section 50 (Interest on delayed payment of tax) provides for interest at a rate not exceeding eighteen per cent as notified. Sections 73 and 74 govern determination of tax not paid, short paid or erroneously refunded, and input tax credit wrongly availed, without and with fraud or wilful misstatement respectively, including show-cause notice procedure. Section 169 specifies the permitted modes of service of notice, order or other communication. Note: this page carries the Act as enacted in 2017; later amendments (for example section 74A inserted for FY 2024-25 onwards) are not reflected and must be checked against current amending Acts and notifications.

sources.publisher: Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs
sources.applicability: Registered persons and GST officers; prescribes the procedural rules for registration, invoicing, input tax credit, returns and payment under the CGST Act.
sources.seedText: Official CBIC PDF of the Central Goods and Services Tax (CGST) Rules, 2017, notified vide Notification No. 3/2017-Central Tax dated 19 June 2017 and stated on its face to be as amended by Notifications No. 7/2017, 10/2017 and 15/2017-Central Tax. It contains the procedural framework for registration, tax invoices, input tax credit, returns and payment of tax under the CGST Act. Note: this document reflects the Rules as they stood at 1 July 2017; the Rules have been amended many times since, so the current amended rule text must be confirmed from a later CBIC notification before relying on a specific procedural requirement.
sources.title: Central Goods and Services Tax (CGST) Rules, 2017 (as notified 19 June 2017)

sources.publisher: Goods and Services Tax Network
sources.title: FAQs on Form GSTR-3B (filing, due dates, nil return, late fee and interest)
sources.applicability: Normal and casual registered taxpayers required to file Form GSTR-3B monthly or quarterly, including those under the QRMP scheme.
sources.seedText: Official GST portal FAQ on Form GSTR-3B. It states that the due date for filing Form GSTR-3B for monthly filers is the 20th day of the month following the month (tax period) to which the return pertains, while for quarterly (QRMP) filers the due date, as notified for different States and UTs, is the 22nd or 24th day of the month following the quarter; the Government may extend the due date by notification. Form GSTR-3B must be filed even if there is no business in the period, and can be filed as a Nil return where there are no transactions and no liability, including late fee, interest or ITC, to report. The FAQ also covers payment of late fee (including carried-forward late fee of the previous tax period), system-computed interest, and Nil filing through the online mode and SMS.

sources.publisher: Goods and Services Tax Network
sources.title: Manual — creating, saving, paying taxes and filing Form GSTR-3B
sources.applicability: Normal registered taxpayers declaring and discharging GST liabilities for a tax period in Form GSTR-3B on the GST portal.
sources.seedText: Official GST portal user manual describing step by step how a taxpayer creates, saves, pays taxes and files Form GSTR-3B. Taxpayers are required to declare their GST liabilities for a tax period and discharge those liabilities in Form GSTR-3B, and a normal taxpayer must file the return for every applicable tax period even if there is no business activity. The manual walks through the return dashboard, auto-population from GSTR-1 and GSTR-2B, tile-wise entry of outward supplies and input tax credit, payment of tax through the electronic cash and credit ledgers, challan creation, and filing with DSC or EVC.

sources.publisher: Employees' Provident Fund Organisation, Ministry of Labour and Employment
sources.title: Present Rates of Contribution (EPF, EPS, EDLI and administrative/inspection charges)
sources.applicability: All establishments covered under the EPF & MP Act, 1952 and their employees; governs monthly statutory payroll deductions and employer liability.
sources.seedText: PRESENT RATES OF CONTRIBUTION. Employee EPF share: 12% (or 10% in specified cases); employee EPS/EDLI: nil. Employer: EPF equals the difference of the employee share and the pension contribution; EPS (A/C 10) 8.33%; EDLI (A/C 21) 0.50%. EPF administrative charges (A/C 2) are 0.50% w.e.f. 01-06-2018, minimum Rs.500 per month per establishment (Rs.75 if there is no contributory member); EDLI administrative charges are nil w.e.f. 01-04-2017. The 10% rate applies to establishments employing fewer than 20 persons, sick industrial companies declared by BIFR, establishments whose accumulated losses equal or exceed their entire net worth, and Jute, Beedi, Brick, Coir and Guar gum factories. Contributions are payable on a maximum wage ceiling of Rs.15,000; contribution on higher wages requires a joint request under Para 26(6) of the EPF Scheme, and the Rs.15,000 ceiling does not apply to International Workers. EPS contribution (8.33%) is paid out of the employer's share and is not payable after the employee crosses 58 years. EDLI contribution is capped at the Rs.15,000 ceiling even if PF is paid on higher wages. Establishments exempted under the PF Scheme pay inspection charges at 0.18% (minimum Rs.5); those exempted under EDLI pay 0.005% (minimum Re.1).

sources.publisher: Income Tax Department, Ministry of Finance
sources.title: TDS Rates chart — Assessment Year 2026-27
sources.applicability: Deductors computing tax deductible at source on payments to residents and non-residents for Assessment Year 2026-27.
sources.seedText: Official Income Tax Department TDS Rates chart page under Tax Charts & Tables, presenting the rates for tax deduction at source for Assessment Year 2026-27, separately for persons other than companies and for companies, with rates to be increased by applicable surcharge and health and education cess where relevant. The chart is organised section-wise across the 192/193/194-series and 195, including salary (192), interest (194A), winnings (194B/194BB), contractor payments (194C), insurance commission (194D), professional and technical fees (194J), rent (194-I), immovable property transfers (194-IA), rent by certain individuals (194-IB), e-commerce (194-O) and purchase of goods (194Q). Read the exact rate and threshold for the specific section and payee status from the chart before computing a deduction.

sources.publisher: Income Tax Department, Ministry of Finance
sources.title: Interest and Fees under the Income-tax Act (sections 234A, 234B, 234C, 234F and TDS/TCS defaults)
sources.applicability: Taxpayers and deductors liable to interest or fees for delayed filing, non-payment or short payment of advance tax, or TDS/TCS defaults.
sources.seedText: Official Income Tax Department tutorial on interest and fees, described as compensatory charges levied automatically without prior notice. Section 234A: 1% per month or part thereof on unpaid tax for delay in filing the return, from the due date to the actual filing date (or to completion of assessment where no return is filed). Section 234B: 1% per month on unpaid tax from 1 April to the date of regular assessment where advance tax paid is less than 90% of the assessed tax. Section 234C: 1% per month for underpayment of the advance-tax instalments benchmarked at 15%, 45%, 75% and 100%. Section 234F fee for late furnishing of the ITR: Rs.1,000 where total income does not exceed Rs.5,00,000 and Rs.5,000 otherwise, with no fee where the assessee is not liable to furnish a return; a fee under section 234-I applies to certain revised returns on the same slabs. For TDS/TCS defaults, section 201/206C interest runs at 1% per month for failure to deduct or collect and 1.5% per month for failure to deposit after deduction or collection. The page also notes situations where interest relief applies, including disputed demands under appeal and income earned abroad that foreign law restricts from remittance.

sources.publisher: Income Tax Department, Ministry of Finance
sources.title: FAQs on Tax Deducted at Source (TDS)
sources.applicability: Deductors and payees seeking official answers on the TDS mechanism, deduction obligations, credit for tax deducted and related compliance.
sources.seedText: Official Income Tax Department FAQ document on Tax Deducted at Source. It explains that for quick and efficient collection of taxes the Income-tax Law incorporates a system of deduction of tax at the point of generation of income, called Tax Deducted at Source, under which the payer deducts tax before making specified payments and deposits it with the Government, with the payee claiming credit for the deducted amount. The FAQs cover the deductor's obligations, the payments covered by the TDS mechanism, and how the payee's credit is reflected. Read the current section-wise rates from the TDS rate chart rather than this FAQ before computing a specific deduction.

sources.publisher: Income Tax Department, Government of India
sources.title: e-Proceedings FAQ — responding electronically to notices, intimations and letters
sources.applicability: Registered e-filing users and their authorised representatives responding to notices, intimations or letters issued by the Income Tax Department.
sources.seedText: Official e-filing portal FAQ on the e-Proceedings service, the electronic platform for conducting proceedings end to end on the e-filing portal. Any registered user or their authorised representative can view and submit a response to any notice, intimation or letter issued by the Income Tax Department. The FAQ describes the benefits of responding electronically — no need to visit the Income Tax Office, easier tracking of submissions and record keeping — the navigation path (log in, then Pending Actions > e-Proceedings), and clarifies mechanics of submitting responses, including that a submitted response does not require separate e-verification.

sources.publisher: Income Tax Department, Government of India
sources.title: e-Proceedings user manual — viewing and responding to income-tax notices
sources.applicability: Taxpayers responding through the e-filing portal to defective-return notices, prima facie adjustments, rectification and notices from the Assessing Officer or CPC.
sources.seedText: Official e-filing portal user manual for the e-Proceedings service, covering notices, intimations and letters issued by the Assessing Officer, CPC or any other Income Tax Authority. It lists the categories that can be viewed and responded to, including defective notice under section 139(9), prima facie adjustment under section 143(1)(a), suo-moto rectification under section 154, notices issued by the Assessing Officer or other authority, and information-seeking notices under sections 133(6) and 131 (including those addressed to another PAN/TAN). The manual gives the step-by-step screens for viewing a notice, submitting a response with attachments, and tracking the proceeding status.

sources.publisher: Income Tax Department, Government of India
sources.title: Reassessment proceedings FAQs — income escaping assessment (section 148, 1961 Act; sections 280-281, 2025 Act)
sources.applicability: Taxpayers who receive reassessment notices where income has escaped assessment, under section 148 of the 1961 Act or the corresponding provisions of the Income-tax Act, 2025.
sources.seedText: Official e-filing portal FAQ on reassessment proceedings. It maps the reassessment framework across the transition from section 148 of the Income-tax Act, 1961 to the new Income-tax Act, 2025, describing the procedure for issuing a notice under section 280 of the 2025 Act where income has escaped assessment for the relevant tax year, including the preliminary information-and-opportunity procedure under section 281. It also explains the circumstances in which the Assessing Officer is not required to follow the section 281 procedure before issuing a section 280 notice, noting that even in such cases approval of the Additional Commissioner or Joint Commissioner is required. Useful for determining which regime and procedural safeguards apply to a reassessment notice received by a client.

sources.publisher: Income Tax Department, Government of India
sources.title: Response to Outstanding Demand — e-filing help and FAQs
sources.applicability: Taxpayers with an outstanding tax demand against their PAN who must pay or contest it through the e-filing portal.
sources.seedText: Official e-filing help page on responding to an outstanding demand. Where the Department finds an outstanding tax demand against a PAN, the taxpayer is given an opportunity to respond; if no response is submitted, the demand is confirmed and adjusted against any refund due or shown as demand payable. Demands are checked by logging in and navigating to Pending Actions > Response to Outstanding Demand, where each demand shows a status of pending payment or response with Pay Now and Submit Response options, and the taxpayer is also alerted by email and SMS. A taxpayer who disagrees in full or in part selects Disagree with demand, chooses from the listed reasons and provides supporting details for each, and is expected to pay the undisputed portion where the disagreement is partial.

"12A. (1) The provisions of section 11 and section 12 shall not apply in relation to

condone such delay and such application shall be deemed to have been filed

chunks.contextHeader: CBDT Circular No. 01/2026 | Power to condone delay in filing Form No. 10A under section 12A(1)(ac)(i) | unit: para 3 | status: active | effective: 2026-03-23 | Trusts and institutions that filed Form 10A late and have a condonation application pending or filed on or after the circular date.
chunks.content:
3.2 References have been received in the Board that a clarification is required as to
whether the jurisdictional Principal Commissioner of Income-tax/Commissioner of
Income-tax or Director of Income-tax (Centralized Processing Centre), Bengaluru would
be the authority to condone the delay in filing application in Form 10A for registration
under section 12A (1)(ac)(i) of the Act.
,.
 4. The Board has examined the matter. In order to avoid genuine hardship to the
eligible trust or institutions and ensure that eligible trusts or institutions are not denied the
benefit of registration solely on account of delay in filing Form No. 10A, the Board, in
exercise of the powers conferred under section 119(2)(b) of the Act, hereby clarifies that
t h e jurisdictional Principal Commissioner of Income-tax or Commissioner of
Income-tax shall have powers to condone delay in filing Form No. 10A under sub-clause
(i) of clause (ac) of sub-section (1) of section 12A of the Act.

chunks.content:
Schedule V [Table: SI. No. 7] of the Income-tax Act, 2025 (hereinafter referred to as the Act)
inter alia provides for exemption to income of a specified person in the nature of dividend , interest, any
sum referred to in section 92(2)(k) of the Act or long-term capital gains (whether or not such capital
ga ins are deemed as sho1t-term capital ga ins under section 76 of the Act) arising from investment made
by it in lndia if the investment is made in specified infrastructure business (including business notified
vide Notification F.No. 13/1 /2 025-IPP dated 19.09.2025, i.e. Infrastructure sub-sectors mentioned in
Harmonised Master List) during the period from O1.04.2020 to 31.03.2030, and held for at least three
years .

GST/INV/DIN-Utility/2022-23 I/116322/2025

Circular No. 249/06/2025-GST
F. No. GST/INV/DIN-Utility/2022-23
Government of India
Ministry of Finance
Department of Revenue
(Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs)

New Delhi, Dated - 09-06-2025.
Subject: Generation and quoting of Document Identiﬁcation Number
(DIN) on any communication issued by the oﬃcers of the Central Board
of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC) to tax payers and other concerned
persons- reg.

Attention is invited to Board's Circular No. 122/41/2019- GST dated 05th
November 2019 and 128/47/2019-GST dated 23.12.2019, which were issued for
implementation of decision regarding Generation and Quoting of Document
Identiﬁcation Number (DIN), initially on speciﬁed documents and subsequently
expanded to all communications (including e-mails) sent to taxpayers and other
concerned persons by any oﬃce of CBIC. This was done with a view to leverage
technology for greater accountability and transparency in communications with the
trade/ taxpayers/ other concerned persons.

chunks.publisher: Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs
chunks.title: DIN requirement for GST common-portal communications carrying a verifiable RFN
chunks.applicability: CBIC communications generated through the GST common portal under section 169 that carry a verifiable Reference Number.
chunks.contextHeader: CBIC Circular No. 249/06/2025-GST | DIN requirement for GST common-portal communications carrying a verifiable RFN | unit: para 2 | status: active | effective: 2025-06-09 | CBIC communications generated through the GST common portal under section 169 that carry a verifiable Reference Number.
chunks.content:
2. It has been brought to the notice of the Board that thedocuments and
summary generated through the common portal of GST always bear a Reference
No. (RFN), which is veriﬁable through the portal
( a t https://services.gst.gov.in/services/verifyRfn). On veriﬁcation, the portal
provides details of the document such as Date of RFN generation, Date of issuing
the Document, Module, Type of Communication and Name of the Oﬃce issuing the
Document.

chunks.publisher: Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs

chunks.applicability: CBIC communications generated through the GST common portal under section 169 that carry a verifiable Reference Number.
chunks.contextHeader: CBIC Circular No. 249/06/2025-GST | DIN requirement for GST common-portal communications carrying a verifiable RFN | unit: para 3 | status: active | effective: 2025-06-09 | CBIC communications generated through the GST common portal under section 169 that carry a verifiable Reference Number.
chunks.content:
3. Reference, in this regard, is also invited to Section 169(1)(d) of the CGST
Act, 2017, which provides that any decision, order, summons, notice or other
communication shall be served by making it available on the common portal.
Further vide Instruction No. 4/2023-GST dated 23.11.2023, CBIC emphasised
on strict compliance of rule 142 of CGST Rules and directed to ensure that
summary of Show Cause Notices in Form GST DRC-01 and summary of the
Order-in-Original in Form GST DRC-07 should be served electronically on common
portal / uploaded electronically on the common portal.

chunks.publisher: Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs
chunks.title: DIN requirement for GST common-portal communications carrying a verifiable RFN
chunks.applicability: CBIC communications generated through the GST common portal under section 169 that carry a verifiable Reference Number.
chunks.contextHeader: CBIC Circular No. 249/06/2025-GST | DIN requirement for GST common-portal communications carrying a verifiable RFN | unit: para 4 | status: active | effective: 2025-06-09 | CBIC communications generated through the GST common portal under section 169 that carry a verifiable Reference Number.
chunks.content:
4. In light of the above, quoting DIN on such communicationsgenerated through
the common portal of GST, which already bear RFN, results into two diﬀerent
electronically generated verifiable unique numbers namely RFN & DIN on the same
communication, which renders quoting of DIN on such communication
unnecessary.
 GST/INV/DIN-Utility/2022-23 I/116322/2025

chunks.publisher: Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs
chunks.title: DIN requirement for GST common-portal communications carrying a verifiable RFN
chunks.applicability: CBIC communications generated through the GST common portal under section 169 that carry a verifiable Reference Number.
chunks.contextHeader: CBIC Circular No. 249/06/2025-GST | DIN requirement for GST common-portal communications carrying a verifiable RFN | unit: para 5 | status: active | effective: 2025-06-09 | CBIC communications generated through the GST common portal under section 169 that carry a verifiable Reference Number.
chunks.content:
5. It is therefore clariﬁed that for communications via common portal (in
compliance with Section 169 of the CGST Act, 2017) having veriﬁable Reference
Number (RFN), quoting of Document Identiﬁcation Number (DIN) is not required
and such communication bearing RFN is to be treated as a valid communication.

chunks.content:
F. No. CBIC-20010/22/2025-GST
Government of India
Ministry of Finance
Department of Revenue
Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs
GST Policy Wing
North Block, New Delhi
Dated: 24th June, 2025

The Principal Chief Commissioners/ Chief Commissioners (All)

The Principal Director General/ Director General (All)

Subject: Reviewing authority, Revisional Authority and Appellate Authority in
respect of orders passed by Common Adjudicating Authority (CAA) for show
cause notices issued by DGGI - reg.

Attention is drawn to notification No. 02/2017 dated 19th June 2017 (as amended) read
with circular No. 239/33/2024-GST dated 04th December 2024, wherein Joint/Additional
Commissioners posted in specified Commissionerates have been designated as Common
Adjudicating Authority (CAA) in respect of show cause notices issued by Directorate General
of GST Intelligence (DGGI). The said circular has specified the procedure to be followed in
case of assigning such show cause notices to the Common Adjudicating Authority along with
their territorial jurisdiction. However, it does not specify the procedure related to review,
revision, and appeals for such Orders-in -Original (O-I-Os) passed by CAA.

chunks.publisher: Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs
chunks.title: Review, revision and appeal for orders passed by Common Adjudicating Authorities
chunks.applicability: Orders-in-Original passed by a Common Adjudicating Authority for show-cause notices issued by DGGI.
chunks.contextHeader: CBIC Circular No. 250/07/2025-GST | Review, revision and appeal for orders passed by Common Adjudicating Authorities | unit: para 2 | status: active | effective: 2025-06-24 | Orders-in-Original passed by a Common Adjudicating Authority for show-cause notices issued by DGGI.
chunks.content:
2. The matter has been examined in consultation with the Union Ministry of Law and
Justice which has clarified that section 107 of the CGST Act, 2017 provides a detailed
mechanism for handling the appeals by the Appellate authority and by exercising the same
power, the rules have also been framed with regard to appeal and review. Similarly, the
Reviewing Authority also has the power under the said section to review adjudication orders
passed by a CAA who is posted under the said reviewing authority.

Page 1 of 3
 3. Similarly, section 108 of the CGST Act, 2017, provides a detailed mechanism for
revision of such orders. Vide notification No. 05/2020-Central tax dated 13th January, 2020, the
jurisdictional Principal Commissioner or Commissioner, as the case may be, has been
authorized as revisional authority for decisions or orders passed by Additional or Joint
Commissioner of Central Tax who are subordinate to him.

chunks.publisher: Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs
chunks.title: Review, revision and appeal for orders passed by Common Adjudicating Authorities
chunks.applicability: Orders-in-Original passed by a Common Adjudicating Authority for show-cause notices issued by DGGI.
chunks.contextHeader: CBIC Circular No. 250/07/2025-GST | Review, revision and appeal for orders passed by Common Adjudicating Authorities | unit: para 4 | status: active | effective: 2025-06-24 | Orders-in-Original passed by a Common Adjudicating Authority for show-cause notices issued by DGGI.
chunks.content:
4. Therefore, to ensure uniformity in procedure for review, revision, and appeal against the
Orders-in-Original (O-I-Os) adjudicated by Common Adjudicating Authorities, it is hereby
clarified that:

a) Review under Section 107 of the CGST Act, 2017: The Principal Commissioner
or Commissioner of Central Tax under whom the Common Adjudicating Authority
(Additional/ Joint Commissioner) is posted shall be the reviewing authority in
respect of such O-I-Os.

b) Revisional Power under Section 108 of the CGST Act, 2017: The Principal
Commissioner or Commissioner of Central Tax under whom the Common
Adjudicating Authority (Additional/ Joint Commissioner) is posted shall be the
revisional authority in respect of such O-I-Os.

c) Appeal Procedure under Section 107 of the CGST Act, 2017: Appeals against
the order of Common Adjudicating Authority (Additional/Joint Commissioner)
shall lie before the Commissioner (Appeals) corresponding to the territorial
jurisdiction of the Principal Commissioner or the Commissioner of Central Tax,
under whom the said Common Adjudicating Authority (Additional/ Joint
Commissioner) is posted, as specified in Table III of notification No. 02/2017-
Central tax dated 19th June, 2017.

d) Department's Representation in Appeals: The Principal Commissioner or
Commissioner of Central Tax of such Commissionerate under whom the Common
Adjudicating Authority (Additional/Joint Commissioner) is posted shall represent
the department in appeal proceedings against the O-I-Os passed by such Common
Adjudicating Authority (Additional/ Joint Commissioner) and accordingly may
appoint any officer subordinate to him to be the designated officer for filing
departmental appeals.

Page 2 of 3
  e) The reviewing or revisional authority for such orders may seek comments on the
O-I-O from the concerned DGGI formation before proceeding to decide on the
order passed by the CAA.

chunks.content:
1. What is Form GSTR-1? Who is required to file Form GSTR-1?

Form GSTR-1 is a monthly/quarterly Statement of Outward Supplies to be furnished by all normal and casual registered taxpayers making outward supplies of goods and services or both and contains details of outward supplies of goods and services.

Every registered taxable person, other than an input service distributor/ composition taxpayer/ persons liable to deduct tax u/s 51 / persons liable to collect tax u/s 52 is required to file Form GSTR-1, the details of outward supplies of goods and/or services during a tax period, electronically on the GST Portal.

chunks.publisher: Goods and Services Tax Network

chunks.applicability: Registered persons preparing or filing outward-supply details in Form GSTR-1 on the GST portal.
chunks.contextHeader: GSTN portal manual | Form GSTR-1 user manual | unit: para 2 | status: active | Registered persons preparing or filing outward-supply details in Form GSTR-1 on the GST portal.
chunks.content:
2. When can I Opt-in for Quarterly Return option for filing of Form GSTR-1 return?

You can opt for Quarterly filing of Form GSTR-1 under following condition:

If your turnover during the preceding financial year was up to Rs. 5 Crore or

If you are registered during the current financial year and expect your aggregate turnover  to be up to Rs. 5 Crores

Note : In case you have chosen  Opt-in for Quarterly Return option, you need to file both Form GSTR-1 and Form GSTR-3B quarterly only.

chunks.content:
3. I have already opted for Quarterly filing of Form GSTR-1 return. Can I change my preference now?

F acility to change frequency is available if you have not filed any return during the financial year according to the original frequency.

4. Is Form GSTR-1 filing mandatory?

Form GSTR-1 needs to be filed even if there is no business activity (Nil Return) in the tax period.

7. Which type of registered taxpayers are not required to file the Form GSTR-1?

The following taxpayers are not required to file Form GSTR-1:

• Taxpayers under the Composition Scheme

• Non-resident foreign tax payers

• Online information database and access retrieval service provider

• Input Service Distributors (ISD)

• Tax Deducted at Source (TDS) (deductors); and

• E-commerce operators collecting TCS

9. For which class of taxpayers is DSC mandatory for filing returns?

DSC is not mandatory for any class of taxpayer as returns can also been filed using EVC.

chunks.content:
10. By when do I need to file the Form GSTR-1 for a given tax period? OR What is the due date for filing the Form GSTR-1?

The due date to file Form GSTR-1 for a given tax period is 11th day of the succeeding month in case of taxpayers filing it monthly and 13th day of month succeeding the end of every quarter in case of taxpayers filing quarterly or such other dates as may be extended by Government through notification.
For example, Form GSTR-1 for the calendar month of January, 2021 needs to be filed by 11th February, 2021. Form GSTR-1 for the quarter of January to March, 2021, needs to be filed by 13th April, 2021.

chunks.publisher: Goods and Services Tax Network
chunks.title: Form GSTR-1 user manual
chunks.applicability: Registered persons preparing or filing outward-supply details in Form GSTR-1 on the GST portal.
chunks.contextHeader: GSTN portal manual | Form GSTR-1 user manual | unit: para 11 | status: active | Registered persons preparing or filing outward-supply details in Form GSTR-1 on the GST portal.
chunks.content:
11. What is the cut-off date to amend details in the invoices for the previous financial year?

The cut-off date to amend details in the invoices for the previous financial year is 30th November of the following financial year. In Form GSTR-1, rectification of error or omission in respect of invoices of the previous financial year will not be allowed after 30th November of the following financial year.

For example, for FY 2022-23, cut-off date for amendment or for adding any missed invoice of FY 2022-23 is 30-Nov-2023.

chunks.content:
12. What does the ‘Total Invoice Value’ column indicate in Form GSTR-1?

The ‘Total Invoice Value’ column in Form GSTR-1 is for the invoice value inclusive of taxes.

chunks.publisher: Goods and Services Tax Network
chunks.title: Form GSTR-1 user manual
chunks.applicability: Registered persons preparing or filing outward-supply details in Form GSTR-1 on the GST portal.
chunks.contextHeader: GSTN portal manual | Form GSTR-1 user manual | unit: para 13 | status: active | Registered persons preparing or filing outward-supply details in Form GSTR-1 on the GST portal.
chunks.content:
13. Will there be any validation on relationship between Invoice value and Taxable Value?

Taxable value is the value as per the provisions of GST law. There will be no validation that the invoice value is equivalent to taxable value plus the tax amount.

chunks.content:
14. Can I enter details of Goods and Services in the same invoice?

Yes, you can enter details of Goods and Services in the same invoices.

B2B supply refers to supply transactions between registered taxable entities/persons (Business-to-Business supplies).

chunks.publisher: Goods and Services Tax Network
chunks.title: Form GSTR-1 user manual
chunks.applicability: Registered persons preparing or filing outward-supply details in Form GSTR-1 on the GST portal.

chunks.content:
16. What is meant by B2C Supplies?

B2C supply refers to supply transactions between a Registered Supplier and an Unregistered Buyer (Business-to-Consumer).

chunks.publisher: Goods and Services Tax Network
chunks.title: Form GSTR-1 user manual
chunks.applicability: Registered persons preparing or filing outward-supply details in Form GSTR-1 on the GST portal.
chunks.contextHeader: GSTN portal manual | Form GSTR-1 user manual | unit: para 17 | status: active | Registered persons preparing or filing outward-supply details in Form GSTR-1 on the GST portal.
chunks.content:
17. When are Debit Notes to be reported in the return?

Debit Notes are to be reported in the return of the month in which they are issued by the supplier.

chunks.publisher: Goods and Services Tax Network
chunks.title: Form GSTR-1 user manual
chunks.applicability: Registered persons preparing or filing outward-supply details in Form GSTR-1 on the GST portal.
chunks.contextHeader: GSTN portal manual | Form GSTR-1 user manual | unit: para 18 | status: active | Registered persons preparing or filing outward-supply details in Form GSTR-1 on the GST portal.
chunks.content:
18. When are Credit Notes to be reported in the return?

Credit Notes are to be reported in the return of the month in which they are issued but not later than the return filed till 30th September following the end of the financial year in which such supply was made, or the date of furnishing of the relevant annual return, whichever is earlier.

chunks.publisher: Goods and Services Tax Network
chunks.title: Form GSTR-1 user manual
chunks.applicability: Registered persons preparing or filing outward-supply details in Form GSTR-1 on the GST portal.
chunks.contextHeader: GSTN portal manual | Form GSTR-1 user manual | unit: para 19 | status: active | Registered persons preparing or filing outward-supply details in Form GSTR-1 on the GST portal.
chunks.content:
19. Does a tax payer need to report the credit notes and debit notes of supplies to consumer separately?

For B2C - Large transactions, credit notes and debit notes need to be reported separately.

For B2C - Small transactions, supplies net of debit notes and credit notes are reported in GSTR-1

chunks.publisher: Goods and Services Tax Network
chunks.title: Form GSTR-1 user manual
chunks.applicability: Registered persons preparing or filing outward-supply details in Form GSTR-1 on the GST portal.
chunks.contextHeader: GSTN portal manual | Form GSTR-1 user manual | unit: para 20 | status: active | Registered persons preparing or filing outward-supply details in Form GSTR-1 on the GST portal.
chunks.content:
20. In case of Receipt of advance by the Supplier from a Receiver, is the supplier liable to pay tax on such an advance amount?

Yes, supplier is liable to pay tax on advances received from receivers for the supply of services and report the consolidated advance received details in a month in which payment is received. The amount of advances to be reported in Form GSTR-1 is net off the amount for which invoices have already been issued and the value reported in the same return in other sections.

chunks.publisher: Goods and Services Tax Network
chunks.title: Form GSTR-1 user manual
chunks.applicability: Registered persons preparing or filing outward-supply details in Form GSTR-1 on the GST portal.
chunks.contextHeader: GSTN portal manual | Form GSTR-1 user manual | unit: para 21 | status: active | Registered persons preparing or filing outward-supply details in Form GSTR-1 on the GST portal.
chunks.content:
21. How is the tax paid on advance payments adjusted against the invoice(s) issued in the subsequent tax period(s)?

The taxpayer has to declare the advance that has to be adjusted in the tax period in which advance is received. Subsequently when invoice is issued, then taxpayer can

adjust the tax liability of the invoice issued of that tax period, in the Form GSTR-1 of that period. This can be shown in the advance adjustment table of Form GSTR-1.

chunks.publisher: Goods and Services Tax Network
chunks.title: Form GSTR-1 user manual
chunks.applicability: Registered persons preparing or filing outward-supply details in Form GSTR-1 on the GST portal.
chunks.contextHeader: GSTN portal manual | Form GSTR-1 user manual | unit: para 22 | status: active | Registered persons preparing or filing outward-supply details in Form GSTR-1 on the GST portal.
chunks.content:
22. How is Export treated under the GST regime?

Exports are generally treated as Zero-rated Inter-State Supplies. In case of exports, the taxpayer has the option to export without payment of any integrated tax and claim refund of ITC (against the exports made) or the taxpayer may pay IGST and claim refund of the IGST amount paid (post affecting the exports).

chunks.publisher: Goods and Services Tax Network
chunks.title: Form GSTR-1 user manual
chunks.applicability: Registered persons preparing or filing outward-supply details in Form GSTR-1 on the GST portal.
chunks.contextHeader: GSTN portal manual | Form GSTR-1 user manual | unit: para 23 | status: active | Registered persons preparing or filing outward-supply details in Form GSTR-1 on the GST portal.
chunks.content:
23. Is shipping bill number mandatory while declaring export invoices in Form GSTR-1?

No, a taxpayer can furnish details of the export invoices in Form GSTR-1 and file the return without mentioning the shipping bill number and date, if the shipping bill details are not readily available with him.

chunks.publisher: Goods and Services Tax Network
chunks.title: Form GSTR-1 user manual
chunks.applicability: Registered persons preparing or filing outward-supply details in Form GSTR-1 on the GST portal.
chunks.contextHeader: GSTN portal manual | Form GSTR-1 user manual | unit: para 24 | status: active | Registered persons preparing or filing outward-supply details in Form GSTR-1 on the GST portal.
chunks.content:
24. How can shipping bill number be furnished after the filing of Form GSTR-1?

If the shipping bill details are received by the taxpayer after the filing of the Form GSTR-1, he needs to declare it in the Form GSTR-1 of the month in which he receives it through the amendment section of Form GSTR-1.

chunks.publisher: Goods and Services Tax Network
chunks.title: Form GSTR-1 user manual
chunks.applicability: Registered persons preparing or filing outward-supply details in Form GSTR-1 on the GST portal.
chunks.contextHeader: GSTN portal manual | Form GSTR-1 user manual | unit: para 25 | status: active | Registered persons preparing or filing outward-supply details in Form GSTR-1 on the GST portal.
chunks.content:
25. How do I report supplies to SEZ units or SEZ developers in Form GSTR-1?

As the SEZ unit or SEZ developer are registered and have GSTIN, the invoice details of supplies to them need to be reported in the section of supplies to registered taxpayers (B2B invoice details) with appropriate SEZ flag.

chunks.publisher: Goods and Services Tax Network
chunks.title: Form GSTR-1 user manual
chunks.applicability: Registered persons preparing or filing outward-supply details in Form GSTR-1 on the GST portal.
chunks.contextHeader: GSTN portal manual | Form GSTR-1 user manual | unit: para 26 | status: active | Registered persons preparing or filing outward-supply details in Form GSTR-1 on the GST portal.
chunks.content:
26. Is it required to submit the details of supplies effected through E-Commerce?

Yes. The return provides for the declaration of the details of all taxable Supplies effected through E-Commerce along with the GSTIN.

chunks.publisher: Goods and Services Tax Network
chunks.title: Form GSTR-1 user manual
chunks.applicability: Registered persons preparing or filing outward-supply details in Form GSTR-1 on the GST portal.
chunks.contextHeader: GSTN portal manual | Form GSTR-1 user manual | unit: para 27 | status: active | Registered persons preparing or filing outward-supply details in Form GSTR-1 on the GST portal.
chunks.content:
27. How should exempt supplies through E-Commerce operator be reported in Form GSTR-1?

It should be reported in a consolidated manner in  table 14 or 14A of form GSTR-1 related to those supplies falls under section 52 or 9(5) of the GST Act.

chunks.publisher: Goods and Services Tax Network
chunks.title: Form GSTR-1 user manual
chunks.applicability: Registered persons preparing or filing outward-supply details in Form GSTR-1 on the GST portal.
chunks.contextHeader: GSTN portal manual | Form GSTR-1 user manual | unit: para 28 | status: active | Registered persons preparing or filing outward-supply details in Form GSTR-1 on the GST portal.
chunks.content:
28. Until when can changes be made to the uploaded invoice details?

Taxpayers can modify/delete invoices any number of times till they submit the Form GSTR-1 of that particular tax period. The uploaded invoice details are in a draft version, and can be changed irrespective of due date until the Form GSTR-1 is filed.

chunks.publisher: Goods and Services Tax Network
chunks.title: Form GSTR-1 user manual
chunks.applicability: Registered persons preparing or filing outward-supply details in Form GSTR-1 on the GST portal.
chunks.contextHeader: GSTN portal manual | Form GSTR-1 user manual | unit: para 29 | status: active | Registered persons preparing or filing outward-supply details in Form GSTR-1 on the GST portal.
chunks.content:
29. Can there be duplicate invoice series in a particular financial year for a particular GSTIN?

For a particular GSTIN, there cannot be duplicate invoice series in a particular financial year. The GST system will not accept duplicate supply invoices in a return and will provide error on validation.

chunks.publisher: Goods and Services Tax Network
chunks.title: Form GSTR-1 user manual
chunks.applicability: Registered persons preparing or filing outward-supply details in Form GSTR-1 on the GST portal.
chunks.contextHeader: GSTN portal manual | Form GSTR-1 user manual | unit: para 30 | status: active | Registered persons preparing or filing outward-supply details in Form GSTR-1 on the GST portal.
chunks.content:
30. Can a registered taxpayer have multiple series of tax invoices?

Yes, a tax payer can have multiple series of tax invoices in a financial year. There is no limit on the number of series of tax invoices that one can have in a financial year.

chunks.publisher: Goods and Services Tax Network
chunks.title: Form GSTR-1 user manual
chunks.applicability: Registered persons preparing or filing outward-supply details in Form GSTR-1 on the GST portal.
chunks.contextHeader: GSTN portal manual | Form GSTR-1 user manual | unit: para 31 | status: active | Registered persons preparing or filing outward-supply details in Form GSTR-1 on the GST portal.
chunks.content:
31. Is there any specified format for invoice number under GST laws?

Yes, the invoice number has to be of maximum length of 16 characters and the allowable characters are alphanumeric and special characters of dash and slash.

chunks.publisher: Goods and Services Tax Network
chunks.title: Form GSTR-1 user manual
chunks.applicability: Registered persons preparing or filing outward-supply details in Form GSTR-1 on the GST portal.
chunks.contextHeader: GSTN portal manual | Form GSTR-1 user manual | unit: para 32 | status: active | Registered persons preparing or filing outward-supply details in Form GSTR-1 on the GST portal.
chunks.content:
32. How HSN wise summary is reported in Form GSTR-1?

From May'25 onwards ,  HSN-wise summary of outward supplies is furnished s eparately for HSN (B2B) and HSN (B2C) along with the rest of the details as required.

From May'21 onwards,  HSN-wise summary of outward supplies  is furnished along with rate and quantitative details.

Before May'21 onwards,  HSN-wise summary of outward supplies is furnished with quantitative details.

chunks.publisher: Goods and Services Tax Network
chunks.title: Form GSTR-1 user manual
chunks.applicability: Registered persons preparing or filing outward-supply details in Form GSTR-1 on the GST portal.
chunks.contextHeader: GSTN portal manual | Form GSTR-1 user manual | unit: para 33 | status: active | Registered persons preparing or filing outward-supply details in Form GSTR-1 on the GST portal.
chunks.content:
33. What is the cut-off date for entry of invoices in Form GSTR-1 in case a normal taxpayer opts for composition scheme?

In cases where a taxpayer opts for composition scheme, Form GSTR-1 will be available for filing only for the period during which the taxpayer was registered as normal taxpayer. The taxpayer would be able to file Form GSTR-1 for the said period, even if filed with delay, for the period prior to opting to composition scheme.

chunks.publisher: Goods and Services Tax Network
chunks.title: Form GSTR-1 user manual
chunks.applicability: Registered persons preparing or filing outward-supply details in Form GSTR-1 on the GST portal.
chunks.contextHeader: GSTN portal manual | Form GSTR-1 user manual | unit: para 34 | status: active | Registered persons preparing or filing outward-supply details in Form GSTR-1 on the GST portal.
chunks.content:
34. From where can I file the Form GSTR-1 and what are the steps involved?

For a detailed description along with screenshots for filing Form GSTR-1, please refer to the User Manual available at help section of the GST Portal.

chunks.publisher: Goods and Services Tax Network

chunks.applicability: Registered persons preparing or filing outward-supply details in Form GSTR-1 on the GST portal.
chunks.contextHeader: GSTN portal manual | Form GSTR-1 user manual | unit: para 35 | status: active | Registered persons preparing or filing outward-supply details in Form GSTR-1 on the GST portal.
chunks.content:
35. What are communications received after successful filing of Form GSTR-1?

a. Application Reference Number (ARN) gets generated on successful filing of Form GSTR-1.

b. An SMS and email is also sent to the taxpayer on the Mobile Number and E mail ID of his primary authorised signatory.

chunks.publisher: Goods and Services Tax Network
chunks.title: Form GSTR-1 user manual
chunks.applicability: Registered persons preparing or filing outward-supply details in Form GSTR-1 on the GST portal.

chunks.content:
36. What are the different ways in which Form GSTR-1 can be electronically signed?

Taxpayers can electronically sign their returns using a DSC or verify through EVC (mandatory for all types of companies and LLPs)

chunks.content:
38. Will a taxpayer receive notice if he does not file Form GSTR-1 by due date?

Yes, he will receive a system generated return defaulter notice in format 3A if he fails to file Form GSTR-1 by due date.

chunks.title: Form GSTR-1 user manual
chunks.applicability: Registered persons preparing or filing outward-supply details in Form GSTR-1 on the GST portal.
chunks.contextHeader: GSTN portal manual | Form GSTR-1 user manual | unit: para 39 | status: active | Registered persons preparing or filing outward-supply details in Form GSTR-1 on the GST portal.
chunks.content:
39. Does a taxpayer need to check the validity of the registration of the recipients furnished in Form GSTR-1?

Yes, the taxpayer should check the validity of the recipients GSTIN and upload the invoice details only if the recipient was active on the date of issue of invoice, otherwise the system will throw a validation error and will not accept invoice details pertaining to that GSTIN.

chunks.publisher: Goods and Services Tax Network

chunks.applicability: Registered persons preparing or filing outward-supply details in Form GSTR-1 on the GST portal.
chunks.contextHeader: GSTN portal manual | Form GSTR-1 user manual | unit: para 40 | status: active | Registered persons preparing or filing outward-supply details in Form GSTR-1 on the GST portal.
chunks.content:
40. Up to how many decimal digits do different values need to be declared in Form GSTR-1?

All values like invoice value, taxable value and tax amounts are to be declared up to 2 decimal digits.

chunks.publisher: Goods and Services Tax Network
chunks.title: Form GSTR-1 user manual
chunks.applicability: Registered persons preparing or filing outward-supply details in Form GSTR-1 on the GST portal.
chunks.contextHeader: GSTN portal manual | Form GSTR-1 user manual | unit: para 41 | status: active | Registered persons preparing or filing outward-supply details in Form GSTR-1 on the GST portal.
chunks.content:
41. A taxpayer cannot file Form GSTR-1 before the end of the current tax period. Is there any exception to this rule?

A taxpayer cannot file Form GSTR-1 before the end of the current tax period. However, following are the exceptions to this rule:

a. Casual Taxpayers after the closure of their business can file Form GSTR-1 before the end of the current tax period

b. A taxpayer who has applied for cancellation of registration will be allowed to file Form GSTR-1 after confirmation of receipt of the application before the end of the current tax period.

chunks.publisher: Goods and Services Tax Network
chunks.title: Form GSTR-1 user manual
chunks.applicability: Registered persons preparing or filing outward-supply details in Form GSTR-1 on the GST portal.
chunks.contextHeader: GSTN portal manual | Form GSTR-1 user manual | unit: para 42 | status: active | Registered persons preparing or filing outward-supply details in Form GSTR-1 on the GST portal.
chunks.content:
42. I am unable to view the invoices, I have uploaded. What should I do?

Scroll down to the bottom of the Form GSTR-1 – Details of outward supplies of goods or services page and click the GENERATE GSTR1 SUMMARY button. This will include the auto drafted details pending for action from recipients. Also the invoices you have added will start reflecting in the relevant section of the Form GSTR-1.

In case you want to see the summary instantly, after you have added the invoices, you can also generate the summary by clicking the GENERATE GSTR1 SUMMARY button. However, summary can be generated only at interval of 10 minutes. In case you attempt to generate summary again (within 10 minutes of earlier generated summary), you may get an error message on top of the page.

The summary is generated by the GST Portal automatically at an interval of every <30 minutes>.

You can also check if any error file has been generated on upload of JSON generated from Offline Tool. If any error file is generated, you can download the error report and rectify the issues using the Offline Tool.

chunks.publisher: Goods and Services Tax Network
chunks.title: Form GSTR-1 user manual
chunks.applicability: Registered persons preparing or filing outward-supply details in Form GSTR-1 on the GST portal.
chunks.contextHeader: GSTN portal manual | Form GSTR-1 user manual | unit: para 43 | status: active | Registered persons preparing or filing outward-supply details in Form GSTR-1 on the GST portal.
chunks.content:
43. The invoice count on the tile summary is different from the number of invoices I had entered/ uploaded. Why?

The invoice count on the tile summary gets updated only after you click the GENERATE GSTR1 SUMMARY button. You can click the GENERATE GSTR1 SUMMARY button to refresh the tile summary.

However, summary can be generated only at interval of 10 minutes. In case you attempt to generate summary again (within 10 minutes of earlier generated summary), you may get an error message on top of the page.

The summary is generated by the GST Portal automatically at an interval of every <30 minutes>.

You can also check if any error file has been generated on upload of JSON generated from Offline Tool. If any error file is generated, you can download the error report and rectify the issues using the Offline Tool.

chunks.publisher: Goods and Services Tax Network
chunks.title: Form GSTR-1 user manual
chunks.applicability: Registered persons preparing or filing outward-supply details in Form GSTR-1 on the GST portal.
chunks.contextHeader: GSTN portal manual | Form GSTR-1 user manual | unit: para 44 | status: active | Registered persons preparing or filing outward-supply details in Form GSTR-1 on the GST portal.
chunks.content:
44. How can I delete or modify the invoices which have been earlier successfully uploaded?

You can click the EDIT/ DELETE button to modify or delete the invoices which have been earlier successfully uploaded. The uploaded invoice details are in a draft version, and can be changed until Form GSTR-1 is filed.

chunks.content:
45. After successfully submitting my Form GSTR-1, I am getting system error when I am affixing my DSC. What should I do?

In case of DSC related issues, click here to know more.

chunks.content:
46. How can I file Nil Form GSTR-1?

You can file nil Form GSTR-1 by first Generating Summary and then submitting the return without entering any data and signing with applicable signature.

chunks.publisher: Goods and Services Tax Network
chunks.title: Form GSTR-1 user manual
chunks.applicability: Registered persons preparing or filing outward-supply details in Form GSTR-1 on the GST portal.
chunks.contextHeader: GSTN portal manual | Form GSTR-1 user manual | unit: para 47 | status: active | Registered persons preparing or filing outward-supply details in Form GSTR-1 on the GST portal.
chunks.content:
47. I have not filed Form GSTR-1 of the previous month, can I file GSTR-1 for the current month?

No, according to section 37(4) of the CGST Act, a taxpayer is not allowed to file GSTR-1 if previous GSTR-1 is not filed. Moreover, according to section 39(10) of the CGST Act, a taxpayer is not allowed to file GSTR-3B if GSTR-1 for the same tax period is not filed.

Further, according to Rule 59(6)(b) a taxpayer is not allowed to file GSTR-1 if previous GSTR-3B is not filed.

chunks.content:
48. When will the Intra-State supplies attracting IGST will be enabled for taxpayers in Form GSTR-1?

Intra-State supplies attracting IGST will be enabled only when the supply attract reverse charge is selected by the taxpayer.

chunks.content:
49. When will all the note supply type checkboxes will be disabled for a taxpayer in Form GSTR-1?

If the recipient GSTIN is ISD GSTIN, then all the note supply type checkboxes will be disabled.

chunks.title: Form GSTR-1 user manual
chunks.applicability: Registered persons preparing or filing outward-supply details in Form GSTR-1 on the GST portal.
chunks.contextHeader: GSTN portal manual | Form GSTR-1 user manual | unit: para 50 | status: active | Registered persons preparing or filing outward-supply details in Form GSTR-1 on the GST portal.
chunks.content:
50. Which GSTINs are allowed as recipient in Form GSTR-1, when taxpayer select note supply type as Deemed Exports?

If the taxpayer selects note supply type as Deemed Exports, then only Normal taxpayer (other than SEZ unit or developer) and Casual taxpayer GSTINs are allowed as recipient.

FAQs > Form GSTR-1 Delinking of Debit and Credit Note

chunks.publisher: Goods and Services Tax Network
chunks.title: Form GSTR-1 user manual
chunks.applicability: Registered persons preparing or filing outward-supply details in Form GSTR-1 on the GST portal.
chunks.contextHeader: GSTN portal manual | Form GSTR-1 user manual | unit: para 1 | status: active | Registered persons preparing or filing outward-supply details in Form GSTR-1 on the GST portal.
chunks.content:
1. Whether taxpayer is required to link the credit or debit note to original invoice?

No, taxpayers can directly report credit or debit notes without linking it to any original invoice.

Before delinking of credit or debit note to original invoice: When the taxpayer issued one credit or debit note, for more than one invoice, then they were not able to enter all these original invoices details in Form GSTR-1. Hence, reporting of the same was not possible.

After delinking of credit or debit note to original invoice: Taxpayers can report single credit or debit note, issued against multiple original invoices in Form GSTR-1, in one go.

chunks.publisher: Goods and Services Tax Network
chunks.title: Form GSTR-1 user manual
chunks.applicability: Registered persons preparing or filing outward-supply details in Form GSTR-1 on the GST portal.
chunks.contextHeader: GSTN portal manual | Form GSTR-1 user manual | unit: para 2 | status: active | Registered persons preparing or filing outward-supply details in Form GSTR-1 on the GST portal.
chunks.content:
2. I have generated the JSON file from old excel utility before delinking, but has not uploaded it on the GST Portal. Can I upload the same now (i.e. after delinking of Debit and Credit Note)?

No, you cannot upload the JSON file generated before delinking of Debit and Credit Note. You need to update the details manually, in new offline excel utility again and then generate the JSON file to upload it into the GST portal.

Note : You need to download latest Returns Offline Tool from the Downloads section of GST Portal. Click here to more about it.

chunks.publisher: Goods and Services Tax Network
chunks.title: Form GSTR-1 user manual
chunks.applicability: Registered persons preparing or filing outward-supply details in Form GSTR-1 on the GST portal.
chunks.contextHeader: GSTN portal manual | Form GSTR-1 user manual | unit: para 3 | status: active | Registered persons preparing or filing outward-supply details in Form GSTR-1 on the GST portal.
chunks.content:
3. I have submitted and filed Form GSTR-1 before delinking. Should I file Form GSTR-1 again after delinking?

If you have already filed Form GSTR-1 before delinking, you are not required to file Form GSTR-1 again, for that period, after delinking.

Note : Taxpayers who have submitted, but not filed, Form GSTR-1 will need to file Form GSTR-1.

Auto-population of e-invoice Details in Form GSTR-1, for taxpayers generating e-invoice

chunks.publisher: Goods and Services Tax Network

chunks.applicability: Registered persons preparing or filing outward-supply details in Form GSTR-1 on the GST portal.
chunks.contextHeader: GSTN portal manual | Form GSTR-1 user manual | unit: para 1 | status: active | Registered persons preparing or filing outward-supply details in Form GSTR-1 on the GST portal.
chunks.content:
1. In which tables of Form GSTR-1 are the details auto-populated from E-invoices?

The data gets auto-populated from E-invoices in the following tables of Form GSTR-1:

a. 4A, 4B, 4C, 6B, 6C – B2B Invoices

c. 9B – Credit/Debit notes (Registered) - CDNR

d. 9B – Credit/Debit notes (Unregistered) - CDNUR

chunks.publisher: Goods and Services Tax Network
chunks.title: Form GSTR-1 user manual
chunks.applicability: Registered persons preparing or filing outward-supply details in Form GSTR-1 on the GST portal.
chunks.contextHeader: GSTN portal manual | Form GSTR-1 user manual | unit: para 2 | status: active | Registered persons preparing or filing outward-supply details in Form GSTR-1 on the GST portal.
chunks.content:
2. Is there a separate link/ tile to view Form GSTR-1 with only the auto populated E-invoice details?

No, there is no separate link/ tile to view Form GSTR-1 only with auto-populated E-invoice details. The details get updated in the existing tile itself. (Perform the same steps to access the Form GSTR-1, Services > Returns > Returns Dashboard option).

chunks.publisher: Goods and Services Tax Network
chunks.title: Form GSTR-1 user manual
chunks.applicability: Registered persons preparing or filing outward-supply details in Form GSTR-1 on the GST portal.
chunks.contextHeader: GSTN portal manual | Form GSTR-1 user manual | unit: para 3 | status: active | Registered persons preparing or filing outward-supply details in Form GSTR-1 on the GST portal.
chunks.content:
3. From where does the data gets auto-populated in Form GSTR-1?

After generating invoices, the taxpayers will upload the invoice details on Invoice Registration Portal (IRP), which in turn will generate a unique invoice reference number (IRN), a QR code and digitally sign it. The GST Portal will get these E-invoice details from IRP and update it in the taxpayer’s Form GSTR-1.

The data gets auto-populated from E-invoices in the following tables of Form GSTR-1:

a. 4A, 4B, 4C, 6B, 6C – B2B Invoices,

c. 9B – Credit/Debit notes (Registered) - CDNR

d. 9B – Credit/Debit notes (Unregistered) - CDNUR

chunks.publisher: Goods and Services Tax Network
chunks.title: Form GSTR-1 user manual
chunks.applicability: Registered persons preparing or filing outward-supply details in Form GSTR-1 on the GST portal.
chunks.contextHeader: GSTN portal manual | Form GSTR-1 user manual | unit: para 1 | status: active | Registered persons preparing or filing outward-supply details in Form GSTR-1 on the GST portal.
chunks.content:
1. Can I edit the details that get auto-populated from E-invoice in Form GSTR-1?

Yes, you can edit the auto-populated E-invoice details in Form GSTR-1.

chunks.publisher: Goods and Services Tax Network
chunks.title: Form GSTR-1 user manual
chunks.applicability: Registered persons preparing or filing outward-supply details in Form GSTR-1 on the GST portal.
chunks.contextHeader: GSTN portal manual | Form GSTR-1 user manual | unit: para 2 | status: active | Registered persons preparing or filing outward-supply details in Form GSTR-1 on the GST portal.
chunks.content:
2. How can I edit the auto-populated E-invoice details in Form GSTR-1?

To edit an E-invoice detail auto-populated in Form GSTR-1, access the invoice ( Dashboard > Returns > Form GSTR-1/ IFF : B2B (or the invoice you wish to edit), and then click the Edit icon available under the Actions column. Click the SAVE button after making the changes in the invoice. Once, the changes are made in invoice, the Source , IRN, and IRN Date fields will become blank.

chunks.publisher: Goods and Services Tax Network
chunks.title: Form GSTR-1 user manual
chunks.applicability: Registered persons preparing or filing outward-supply details in Form GSTR-1 on the GST portal.
chunks.contextHeader: GSTN portal manual | Form GSTR-1 user manual | unit: para 3 | status: active | Registered persons preparing or filing outward-supply details in Form GSTR-1 on the GST portal.
chunks.content:
3. Is there any additional field/ column that gets displayed for E-invoices auto-populated in Form GSTR-1?

Yes, in case the E-invoice details are auto-populated in Form GSTR-1, the following columns get displayed in the Processed Documents page:

• Source : Displays the source from where the details are uploaded in Form GSTR-1. ‘E-invoice’ implies that the details are auto-populated from E-invoice.

• IRN : Invoice Reference Number (IRN) of the E-invoice.

• IRN Date : Date of E-invoice.

chunks.title: Form GSTR-1 user manual

chunks.contextHeader: GSTN portal manual | Form GSTR-1 user manual | unit: para 4 | status: active | Registered persons preparing or filing outward-supply details in Form GSTR-1 on the GST portal.
chunks.content:
4. How do I update the changes made in auto-populated E-invoice details in my Form GSTR-1?

To update the changes, click EDIT > Change Details > Save records and then click the GENERATE SUMMARY button available at the bottom of Form GSTR-1 page to update invoice details.

D ownloading/ Viewing E-invoice Details in Form GSTR-1
